sections.h2: What should a seller know about Pierce County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Pierce County is a rural southeast Georgia county with Blackshear as its seat. The county government says it was established in 1857 from land that belonged to Appling and Ware counties, and it was named for President Franklin Pierce. The Alabaha River winds through it, and its website points visitors toward fishing and the history of the Okefenokee.

It is the most spread-out county in the four-county Census comparison. Mid-2025 population is estimated at 20,764, which is 5.3 percent above the 2020 base, spread across 340.46 square miles of land. That works out to 57.9 people per square mile in 2020. The county issued only 68 building permits in 2025, the fewest of the four compared, so a resale competes with little new housing.

Prices reflect that. A typical owner-occupied house is valued at $153,300, based on 2020 to 2024 data. Owners live in 76.5 percent of homes, and renters pay a median of $799 a month. Median household income was $60,517, and 82.9 percent of households have broadband. At these values, back taxes can eat a big slice of a sale price, so a seller gains from learning the balance early.

sections.h2: Which Pierce County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Two offices share the work, the Tax Commissioner and the Board of Assessors, and both have addresses on Nichols Street in Blackshear. The commissioner's page describes an office independent of the assessors and of the county commissioners, who control only its budget. The commissioner's main duty is to collect the taxes the assessors set.

The commissioner takes property tax payments online, and the site says online payments post on the next business day. Cards other than American Express are accepted with a convenience fee. A Georgia driver's license with a Pierce County address is required to title or tag a vehicle in the county.

sections.h2: What did the 2025 Pierce County millage notice say?
sections.html:
The county's millage page carries a notice that the Board of Commissioners tentatively adopted a 2025 rate requiring a property tax increase of 19.98 percent for unincorporated areas and 20.20 percent for incorporated areas. The hearings were held at the NFC Building at 705 College Avenue in Blackshear on November 6 and November 13, 2025, and those dates have passed.

That page also links the 2025 digest with its five-year levy history, plus the prior year's digest. Three authorities set millage: the commissioners, the school board and the State. Because the final rate can differ from a tentative one, ask the commissioner which millage appears on your bill, and ask whether your parcel sits in Blackshear, Patterson or an unincorporated area.

sections.h2: When is Pierce County property tax due?
sections.html:
The due date is printed on your bill, and the Tax Commissioner can confirm it. The state revenue department's county facts page explains the range. December 20 is the official date, yet a county can pass a resolution for December 1 or November 15, or can split billing into installments.

State rules give you some breathing room, and a few other facts help sellers:

  • Interest cannot start until 60 days after the bill's postmark, according to the state's county facts page, and penalties may follow on delinquent balances.
  • Pierce County property is taxed to the owner as of January 1.
  • The return window at the county tax office runs January 1 to April 1.
  • A mobile home sitting in the county on January 1 needs its return filed by April 1, and the location permit is handled at the same time.

The commissioner's site also lists a tax sale registration form and an excess funds list. If your parcel is behind on payments, call 912.449.2026 before you list so you know how much to pay off at closing.

sections.h2: How does a Pierce County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
After the assessors set a new value, a notice goes to the taxpayer, who has 45 days to appeal in writing. The assessor's FAQ says late appeals are invalid. An appeal may rest on taxability, uniformity or value.

The appeal runs in stages:

  • The Board of Assessors reviews the appeal first and decides whether a change is warranted.
  • If the value stands, the Pierce County Grand Jury's appointees on the three-person Board of Equalization hear the dispute next.
  • Either side may take the decision to Pierce County Superior Court.

Appraisers work from three methods (cost, comparable sales and income). Field staff may stop at a parcel to look into an appeal, a return, a new addition or a conservation application. Visitors from the office show photo identification and arrive in a marked county vehicle. To meet with the Board of Assessors, book by the Friday before its 9:00 a.m. session; the board sits at least twice monthly.

sections.h2: What exemptions and special assessments apply in Pierce County?
sections.html:
The Pierce County homestead exemption is available at the assessors' office year-round, but it must be filed by April 1 to reduce the current year's bill. Ownership and residence on January 1 are required, which pushes a house bought later in the year to the following year. Once granted, it stays in place until you move or the ownership changes. The Georgia Department of Revenue's county page says no local homestead exemptions are offered, so state exemptions are what applies; ask the assessors what your age or veteran status adds.

The assessor's FAQ lists special programs that can lower the value of land:

  • Preferential farm property is taxed on 30 percent of market value rather than 40, in return for a 10-year commitment.
  • Conservation use assessment values bona fide farm and forest land at current use value.
  • Environmentally sensitive property and residential transitional property can also use current use value.
  • Trees on the stump escape tax until they are sold or cut, then count at full market value.

A seller of acreage under a covenant should ask the assessors how a sale or a change in use affects the agreement before signing a contract. The county has 57.9 people per square mile, so farm and timber parcels are a real part of its sales, and the covenant terms are worth requesting in writing.

faqs.q: Where is the Pierce County Tax Commissioner's office?
faqs.a: It is at 312 Nichols Street, Suite 4, in Blackshear, Georgia, with hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. Monday through Friday. The phone is 912.449.2026.

faqs.q: What is the Pierce County property tax due date?
faqs.a: Ask the commissioner or check your bill. Georgia's standard date is December 20, though a county may choose December 1 or November 15, or bill in installments.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Pierce County assessment?
faqs.a: Put it in writing within 45 days of the notice date. The assessors' FAQ calls any later appeal invalid.

faqs.q: Can I pay Pierce County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. The commissioner accepts major cards except American Express, with a convenience fee, and online payments post on the next business day.

faqs.q: When must a Pierce County homestead exemption be filed?
faqs.a: By April 1 of the year you want the exemption. You have to have owned the property and lived there on January 1 of that year.
